entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Guillaume d'Aure, OSB, was a French Benedictine monk and Cardinal born in Toulouse, France, and died on 3 December 1353 in Avignon.

 He was the son of Bernard VII Dodon, Count of Comminges, and Bertrande, Countess d'Aure, daughter of Arnaud, Vicomte de l'Arboust, making him a member of the noble Dodon family.

 As a prominent figure in the Catholic Church, d'Aure played a crucial role in the Avignon Papacy, serving as a cardinal and participating in the conclave that elected Pope Clement VI.

 His legacy extends beyond his religious influence, as he was a key figure in the governance of the region during a time of great turmoil.

 In the annals of history, Guillaume d'Aure stands as a testament to the enduring power of faith and leadership in shaping the course of human events.
